signature_level_breaks_found_that_the_li: **Four public Rust read verbs gained a REQUIRED parameter.** `Engine::read_get`, `Engine::read_get_many`, `Engine::read_list` and `Engine::graph_neighbors` each gained `view: &ReadView`. **Edge `t_valid`/`t_invalid` retyped ISO-8601 String -> INTEGER epoch seconds (TC-33).** `PreparedWrite::Edge` fields moved Option<String> -> Option<i64>, and the GOVERNED SDK WRITE SURFACE moved with them in all three languages (napi lib.rs:2476-2487 `json_i64_alt`, replacing a `json_str_alt` that did no format validation at all; fathomdb-py lib.rs:2097-2106 `dict_epoch_seconds`). Neither SDK names the field in a typed stub (write items are loose maps), so nothing in the symbol diff catches it. This is a silent runtime break for any caller passing an ISO-8601 edge timestamp, and it is the same change that costs the edge data at step 23. Now its own Changed — BREAKING entry, cross-linked to the upgrade warning.

**`EngineError` gained 6 variants and is NOT `#[non_exhaustive]`** (derive at lib.rs:3556 carries no non_exhaustive): Consolidator, ErasureIncomplete, IllegalTransition, NotLifecycleAddressable, ProjectionDestructive, VectorEquivalenceMismatch. known_issues_included.why_consumer_observable: p1, open, verified (seq 128/145). Engine::transition is a PUBLIC SDK verb that fails 10/10 under stress with a plain SQLITE_BUSY, busy handler invoked zero times, in 0ms against a 5000ms timeout, and never emits a diagnostic code — so the caller gets an opaque StorageError indistinguishable from a permanent failure and no busy_timeout setting helps. Included with a workaround (serialise or retry) and the 0.8.21 schedule.

p2, open, verified (seq 129). `let _ = commit_projection_outcomes(..)` means a projection worker can fail to persist with NO error, log or telemetry — a caller relying on eventual search/vector freshness gets no signal. Included with the workaround (assert freshness via vector_dense_readiness + a drain barrier). Its other half (the ~50% baseline duplicate-embed rate) is wasted compute, not a correctness bug, and was deliberately left out.
p2, open, verified (seq 136). A Python or TypeScript caller literally cannot recover which bounds (or which ProjectionSpec) were rejected.
An operator who sized `cap` against a physical row count now gets a different table size. Cross-referenced, not duplicated.

p2 both. The PUBLIC Engine::drain can burn its full timeout and return an indistinguishable Err(Scheduler) — during a freeze window, and via a lost-wakeup race measured at 30.19s vs 0.25s on the same test across parallel runs. A short drain timeout can fail spuriously. Merged into one entry because the consumer-visible symptom is identical.
A TypeScript binding footgun with a concrete remedy: napi omits the property for Option::None rather than emitting null, so `=== null` silently misses. Included with 'test with == null or ??'.

p2. A BYO-LLM-extracted edge timestamp of 2025-02-30 is stored as a DIFFERENT, WRONG instant (2025-03-02). Data-correctness, not cosmetic. Included with the honest safety bound (always a real instant, never NULL, so the no-resurrection-via-NULL property holds — wrong-instant, not fail-open).

p1, verified. Erasure correctness is exactly what a consumer deserves to be told about.
